learning_outcomes.text: To familiarize themselves with the fundamental principles of magnetism
To know very well the methodology of solving problems related to magnetic materials.
To be able to use this knowledge to solve physical problems.
Strengthen the theoretical background to understand fundamental principles of Magnetism.
Develop critical thinking in solving problems in Magnetism and Magnetic Materials

syllabus_topics: Magnetic moment, Magnetization, Special Magnetization, Magnetic susceptibility
Paramagnetism: Classical and a Quantum theory
Low dimensional interactions, Spin glass, super-paramagnetism
assessment_rules: Students are evaluated through an optional mid-term exam and a final examination. The final examination includes theory and problem-solving. Students have the right to review their exam and ask questions. The weights for the optional mid-term exam (30%) and final examination (70%) are specified, but the conditional nature of the optional exam implies ambiguous total weighting if the mid-term is not taken.
bibliography: B.D. Cullity and C.D. Graham, “Introduction to Magnetic Materials”, 2nd edition, Willey, and IEEE.
Notes from the instructor on the course’s website.
David Jiles, “Introduction to Magnetism and magnetic Materials”, 2nd edition, Chapman & Hall (1998)
degree: Materials Science and Engineering — Πτυχίο Τμήματος Επιστήμης και Μηχανικής Υλικών (first cycle, 240 ECTS, curriculum ΕΜΥ)
